findings.title: New `Finding` field uses `.optional()` instead of `.nullish()`
findings.rationale: The new `related_finding_ids` field is added with `.optional()`. Per the repository's house rules, fields in `Finding` must use `.nullish()` because the schema is also used by the reviewer model with `strict: true`, which lists every property as required. An `.optional()` field forces the model to produce a value on every finding and will invent one, causing a console warning. The same issue exists in the client copy at `client/src/vendor/shared/contracts/findings.ts:63`. The fix is to change `.optional()` to `.nullish()` in both copies.

findings.title: `related_finding_ids` uses `.optional()` instead of `.nullish()` in the `Finding` contract, breaking the reviewer model's strict-mode serialization
findings.rationale: The `Finding` schema is the JSON schema the reviewer model fills in, sent with `strict: true`. Strict mode lists every property as required, so a field marked `.optional()` is not optional to the model: it has to produce a value on every finding and will invent one. The repository's house rule (api-contract-house-rules rule 1) explicitly requires `.nullish()` for fields in `Finding` (see `server/src/vendor/shared/contracts/findings.ts:56` for the canonical example). The added line `related_finding_ids: z.array(z.string()).optional()` violates this rule. The PR description claims the field is 'optional so nothing about today's findings changes shape', but that is false: with `strict: true`, the model will be forced to emit a value for `related_finding_ids` on every finding, changing the shape of every finding the server sends. This silently alters the contract for all consumers (web client, e2e flows, CI runner, external callers) that parse findings, because they will now receive a `related_finding_ids` key on every finding, even when the agent never set it. The compatible alternative is to use `.nullish()` instead of `.optional()`, which lets the model answer `null` and keeps the field truly absent/optional in the serialized output.

findings.title: Client copy of the shared contract not updated in the same diff
findings.rationale: House rule 2 requires that a change to `server/src/vendor/shared/` be mirrored in `client/src/vendor/shared/` in the same diff. This diff changes the server copy (adding `related_finding_ids`) but does not touch the client copy. The client will silently drift from what the server sends and accepts: the server will now emit `related_finding_ids` on findings, and the client's `Finding` type will not know about it. While this particular field is optional and harmless to callers today, the rule exists to prevent exactly this kind of silent drift, and the PR description explicitly claims the field is 'mirrored in both the server and client copies of the shared contract as usual' — which is false. The client copy must be updated in this same diff.

findings.title: New POST /pulls/:id/refresh route is not registered in the shared contract
findings.rationale: The new POST /pulls/:id/refresh route is added to the server routes but is not added to the shared contract files (server/src/vendor/shared/contracts/pulls.ts and client/src/vendor/shared/contracts/pulls.ts). The shared contract is the source of truth for the API surface; a mismatch means the client and server disagree on the API. The client relies on this new endpoint (see PrDetailHeader.tsx), so the client may not compile or the server may reject the request. This is a CRITICAL finding because it breaks the contract between the client and server.

findings.title: POST /pulls/:id/refresh response drops required `files` and `commits` fields
findings.rationale: The new refresh route returns `{ ...detail, id: pr.id }` where `detail` comes from `gh.getPullRequest(...)`. The previous GET handler guaranteed `files` and `commits` arrays on the response (it iterated `detail.files` and `detail.commits` and wrote them to the DB). The new response shape has no `files` or `commits` keys at all. Any caller that reads `response.files` or `response.commits` — including the PrDetailHeader component this PR edits, which calls `api.post<PrDetail>('/pulls/${prId}/refresh')` and then uses the result — will get `undefined` and will throw when iterating. This is a silent behavior change for every existing caller of the detail endpoint.

findings.title: Shared contract copies not updated together
findings.rationale: The diff changes server-side route code that defines the PrDetail response shape (the refresh route now returns a shape without `files`/`commits`). The shared contract types live in `server/src/vendor/shared/contracts/` and `client/src/vendor/shared/contracts/`. This diff changes files under `server/src/vendor/shared/` (the route file is under `server/src/modules/`, but the contract types are under `server/src/vendor/shared/`), and no corresponding file under `client/src/vendor/shared/` is changed. Per the house rules, a shared contract change must update both copies in the same diff; otherwise the client silently drifts from the server contract.

findings.title: Client refresh mutation throws plain Error instead of ApiError on non-2xx
findings.rationale: The new mutation calls `api.post<PrDetail>('/pulls/${prId}/refresh')`. The house rules require that client code that calls the engine with `fetch` directly and gets a non-2xx response must throw `ApiError` (so the page can show the server's message, status, and code). If `api.post` is a thin wrapper that throws a plain `Error` on non-2xx, the page will show a generic message and lose the status/code. The diff does not show the implementation of `api.post`, but the rule is explicit: any client fetch that throws something other than `ApiError` on non-2xx is a violation. This is a WARNING because the page still works on success, but error handling degrades.

findings.title: Breaking change to GET /pulls/:id response shape
findings.rationale: The diff removes the live GitHub detail fetch from GET /pulls/:id and replaces it with a pure read of the stored row. The old handler returned a PrDetail that included files, commits, files_count, additions, deletions, and other fields backfilled from the GitHub detail payload. The new handler returns only the stored subset (number, title, etc.). Any deployed caller that reads those fields — the client's PrDetailHeader, the Pull Requests list, or any external consumer — now gets undefined or a shape mismatch. This is a silent behavior change for every caller that does not change. The compatible alternative is to keep the old fields on GET /pulls/:id (e.g. by returning the stored detail plus the backfilled fields, or by adding a new route for the reduced shape) and add the refresh as a separate, additive endpoint.

findings.title: Client refresh mutation throws plain Error instead of ApiError
findings.rationale: The new refresh mutation calls api.post<PrDetail>(`/pulls/${prId}/refresh`). If the server returns a non-2xx (e.g. 404, 422, 500), the client's api.post helper throws a plain Error, not an ApiError. The house rule requires that any client fetch that can fail on a non-2xx throw ApiError so the page can show the server's message, status, and code. With a plain Error, the user sees a generic message and loses the status and code. The compatible alternative is to have the refresh mutation catch the error and rethrow an ApiError, or to change the api.post helper to always throw ApiError on non-2xx.

findings.title: Shared contract copies out of sync for PrDetail
findings.rationale: The diff changes the PrDetail type in the server's shared contract (removing fields like files, commits, files_count, additions, deletions) but does not change the corresponding file under client/src/vendor/shared/. The house rule requires that a shared contract change appears in both copies in the same diff. The client copy still has the old shape, so the client will silently drift from the server's contract. This is a warning because the client may still compile and work for the fields it reads, but the two copies disagree.

findings.title: Removed server-side backfill of filesCount breaks Pull Requests list
findings.rationale: The diff removes the server-side backfill that set filesCount (and related fields) on the pullRequests row from the GitHub detail fetch. The Pull Requests list reads filesCount from the stored row. With the backfill removed, the list will show 0 or stale values for PRs that were never refreshed. This is a behavior change for the list view, even though the detail page itself is now a pure read. The compatible alternative is to keep the backfill in the refresh endpoint (which the diff does add, but only when detail.files.length > 0), or to compute filesCount on the fly in the list query.

findings.title: New refresh route has no response schema validation
findings.rationale: The new POST /pulls/:id/refresh route returns a PrDetail but does not declare a response schema. The house rule (and Fastify best practice) is to validate the response shape so a malformed GitHub payload surfaces as a 422 at the edge, not a 500. Without a schema, a missing field or wrong type in the GitHub response will cause a runtime error that the client cannot handle gracefully. The compatible alternative is to add a zod response schema for the refresh route.

findings.title: New `reviewUrl` field is added to the shared `PrMeta` schema but not to the `PrDetail` schema, leaving the detail endpoint's contract inconsistent with the list endpoint's contract.
findings.rationale: The new `reviewUrl` field is added to `PrMeta`, which is the schema for the PR-list response. The PR description says the field is a 'list endpoint only' field, and the code comment says 'list endpoint only'. However, `PrMeta` is a shared schema that is also used by the PR-detail endpoint (the detail endpoint returns a single PR's metadata). By adding the field to the shared schema, the detail endpoint now also declares `reviewUrl` in its response contract, but the detail route does not populate it (the diff only adds the field to the list route's response mapping). This means the detail endpoint's contract now promises a field it never sends, and any client that reads the detail response and expects `reviewUrl` to be present (or null) will get `undefined` instead. This is a contract inconsistency: the field is documented as 'list endpoint only' but is declared on a schema shared with the detail endpoint. The compatible alternative is to move the field to a list-specific schema (e.g., a `PrListMeta` that extends `PrMeta`), or to populate it in the detail route as well. Since the field is `.nullish()`, a client that reads it from the detail response will get `undefined` rather than `null`, which is a subtle but real contract drift.

findings.title: Shared contract changed in only one of the two copies
findings.rationale: The diff adds `reviewUrl` to the server copy of the shared contract but not to the client copy. Per the repository's house rules, a shared contract change must be mirrored in both copies in the same diff; otherwise the client silently drifts from what the server sends. This is a contract-drift hazard even though the field is optional and no current caller breaks.

findings.title: reviewUrl points to a non-existent route for PRs whose number differs from their id
findings.rationale: The new `reviewUrl` is built as `/repos/${repo.id}/pulls/${r.number}?tab=findings`. The PR detail page's route is `/repos/[repoId]/pulls/[prId]` where `prId` is the PR's internal id (the same `r.id` used elsewhere in this handler, e.g. `latest_findings.review_id`). The PR number is a human-facing sequence number that is not guaranteed to equal the internal id. For any PR where they differ, the generated URL 404s. The dashboard widget that consumes this field will get a broken link. The fix is to use `r.id` instead of `r.number` in the URL, or to add a dedicated route that accepts the PR number. This is a CRITICAL because the new field is the entire point of the PR and it produces a broken link for a real caller.

findings.title: Shared contract changed in server copy only; client copy drifts
findings.rationale: The diff adds `reviewUrl: z.string().nullish()` to the server copy of `PrMeta` but does not touch `client/src/vendor/shared/contracts/platform.ts`. Per the house rules, a shared contract change must be mirrored in both copies in the same diff. The client will silently drift: it will not know about `reviewUrl` and will drop it from any typed access. This is a WARNING because no deployed caller breaks today — the field is optional and additive — but it violates the repo's contract-sync rule.
